new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (text layer present; extracted text of PDF p.16 = book p.10, Chapter 2 'The sound system', sec. 2.2 'Introduction'). The sentence is there verbatim: 'As far as suprasegmentals are concerned, tone and stress have no contrastive function, stress being approximately equal on all syllables. Furthermore, there are no elaborate morphophonemic changes.' Sec. 1.6 'Sketch of Imonda' (p.8, PDF p.14) also verbatim: 'It has no phonologically relevant tones and no elaborate morphophonemics.' The 1984 ANU thesis PDF p.31 = p.20 carries the identical suprasegmental sentence. a full-text search for stress/accent the full text for stress/accent/prominence/suprasegmental/intonation finds no other word…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Seiler reports no contrastive stress or tone in Imonda; stress is described as roughly even across all syllables of the word, i.e. no fixed or lexical stress position is posited.
new_statements.exceptions: None. Author caveat (sec. 2.1, p.10): the phonology chapter covers 'only the main points of the sound system' since the work's emphasis is morphosyntax; vowel reduction of schwa-like vowels in polysyllabic words is mentioned (p.11ff) but not tied to stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level impressionistic statement; no instrumental data. Intonation contours are discussed only at clause level (ch.9) without reference to word stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Seiler describes Imonda as spoken in Imonda village (and post-1962 a second nearby village), West Sepik (Sandaun) Province; matches glottocode imon1245 directly, no dialect split. He notes age-graded (old vs young) pronunciation variation only.
